title: Balbus et al. (2019)
headline: Theorem 1(i) is false under the order assumptions as printed, and the appendix contains an independent function-space defect.

work.title: A Qualitative Theory of Large Games with Strategic Complementarities

claims.label: Theorem 1(i)
claims.gist: Under Assumption 1, greatest and least distributional equilibria exist.
claims.statement: Under Assumption 1, there exists a greatest and a least distributional equilibrium of the game.
conditions: compact perfect Hausdorff type space with a regular singleton-null probability measure
the printed partial-order condition that pair comparison implies action comparison
quasisupermodularity, single-crossing differences and the stated Carathéodory condition
claims.quantifiers: Every game admitted by the standing framework and Assumption 1.

result.summary: The literal one-way order condition admits a game satisfying Assumption 1 with no distributional equilibrium.
result.witness: Take types [0,1] with Lebesgue probability, actions {0,1}, a constant feasible-action set, and equality as the partial order on type-action pairs. Let p be the mass choosing action 1. Make action 1 uniquely optimal when p<1/2 and action 0 uniquely optimal when p≥1/2. Equality is permitted by the printed one-way order condition and makes the induced stochastic order equality, so the single-crossing condition is vacuous. Any equilibrium with p<1/2 would force p=1; any equilibrium with p≥1/2 would force p=0. Hence no distributional equilibrium exists.
result.tested: The exact assumption matrix, the induced stochastic order, strict best replies and the equilibrium contradiction were checked in a separate informed hostile validation. A strengthened four-action witness also defeats the possible rescue that greatest/least feasible distributions or chain completeness were intended as additional premises.
not_claimed: The record does not claim that the authors' intended stronger order condition is false.
Applications that independently impose a product or same-type action order are not claimed to fail.
No downstream paper is claimed to be incorrect without checking its own assumptions.
result.repair_note: A same-type fiber condition requiring action order to imply pair order excludes the counterexample and supplies a comparison used in the proof. The appendix chain-completeness argument still needs a separate valid justification.

vor_check.detail: The canonical source lock is partial because the historical decisive check used extracted final publisher text rather than a complete rendered-page verification. The theorem wording and order assumptions were rechecked on the publisher-hosted article during release preparation.

checks.detail: A separate informed hostile-validation session reconstructed the assumptions, tested rescue attempts and confirmed the exact counterexample.
A qualifying human confirmation is recorded in the private research file. Its source and correspondence are not disclosed.

claims.label: Lemma A1 proof: function-space step
claims.gist: The proof treats M(X)-M(X), where M(X) contains bounded measurable isotone functions, as a Riesz subspace of C(X).
claims.statement: In the proof of Lemma A1, M(X)-M(X) is asserted to be a Riesz subspace of the continuous functions C(X).
conditions: X is a compact Hausdorff partially ordered space
M(X) is defined as the bounded measurable isotone real-valued functions on X
claims.quantifiers: The appendix argument is presented for the stated general class of compact ordered spaces and regular measures.

result.summary: Measurability and isotonicity do not imply continuity, so the asserted inclusion in C(X) does not follow.
result.witness: Under the equality order, every bounded measurable function is isotone. Discontinuous indicator functions therefore belong to M(X), so M(X) and M(X)-M(X) need not be contained in C(X). The Stone-Weierstrass step cannot be justified from the displayed definition as written.
result.tested: The appendix definitions and the claimed Riesz-subspace step were traced in the historical audit and independently attacked in the hostile validation.
not_claimed: This defect alone is not claimed to falsify the conclusion of Lemma A1.
The record does not claim that no alternative proof of the relevant measure-order result exists.
The record does not publish or rely on any private proposed correction.
result.repair_note: The function class or the proof must be strengthened so that the functions used in the Stone-Weierstrass argument are continuous; a complete repair of the constrained-measure chain-completeness argument is not claimed here.

vor_check.detail: The canonical source lock is partial because the historical check used extracted final publisher text. The publisher-hosted article was rechecked during release preparation and still defines M(X) as measurable and bounded before asserting the subspace inclusion.

checks.detail: A separate informed hostile-validation session confirmed the mismatch between the displayed definition of M(X) and the continuity required by the proof.
A qualifying human confirmation is recorded in the private research file. Its source and correspondence are not disclosed.
